title: Catan agent lab
headline: Winning games is the objective. Keep the strongest measured policy in play while every new idea earns promotion on fresh, paired games.
current_agent: OneVOne for the provisional 1v1 Catanatron arena
current_result: 1,474 / 2,056 wins (71.7%) against the pinned web bot on the 1,028-board diagnostic grid
rules: 1v1 tests: two players, 10 VP, official spiral, discard at 7, no friendly robber. Four-player tests are a separate arena and are never pooled with 1v1 rates.
evaluation_note: The 1,028-board grid reuses dataset board seeds, so it is a broad diagnostic rather than an independent holdout. Fresh confirmation and direct head-to-head runs are labeled separately.
next_gate: A candidate must beat OneVOne on fresh board seeds, from both seats, with legal moves, no game caps, and a paired win-rate improvement before promotion.

experiments.title: External-teacher trajectory set
experiments.comparison: Value Base, Value Contender and Victory Point teachers
experiments.finding: Each row stores a visible observation, legal actions, the chosen teacher action and final outcome. The games are not fixed move scripts for later agents to replay.
experiments.decision: Useful for imitation and state-value diagnostics; win rate still needs new games.

experiments.title: OneVOne incumbent
experiments.comparison: Pinned Catanatron web bot; 1,028 boards × both seats
experiments.finding: Production, expansion, hand value, robber pressure and deterministic VP conversion are scored together. This remains the strongest profile on the broad 1v1 grid.
experiments.decision: Keep as the 1v1 benchmark and playable agent.

experiments.title: Mutating OneVOne weights
experiments.comparison: 32 boards, four opponent types, both seats
experiments.finding: Two seeded searches over value, robber and search parameters selected the unchanged baseline. Sampled mutations did not improve paired held-out wins.
experiments.decision: No trained configuration was promoted.

experiments.title: Five-head MLP from mixed teachers
experiments.comparison: Larger 768-game, 64-board training corpus
experiments.finding: Family accuracy reached 86.8%, but choosing a broad action family did not reliably choose its legal target. Earlier 16-board training scored 1/64 versus the web bot.
experiments.decision: Do not replace the heuristic with this imitation policy.

experiments.title: Legal-action MLP from Catanatron teachers
experiments.comparison: Pinned web bot on the planner confirmation schedule
experiments.finding: The policy matched teachers on many easy choices but often ended turns with usable cards, missed development purchases, and lagged in production and VP.
experiments.decision: Teacher agreement is not the promotion metric.

experiments.title: Short PPO fine-tune
experiments.comparison: Matched sealed mixed-bot screen
experiments.finding: Terminal win/loss training on a small run did not repair rare development purchases or the midgame expansion gap.
experiments.decision: PPO checkpoint was not promoted; this does not rule out longer or better-shaped RL.

experiments.title: Action-type calibration
experiments.comparison: Frozen MLP plus a learned residual and End Turn adjustment
experiments.finding: Held-out Buy Development matches moved from 0/173 to 78/173. The win gain came largely against weaker opponents; Value Base improved only 1/26 to 3/26.
experiments.decision: Useful targeted repair, insufficient as a standalone agent.

experiments.title: Settlement-location reranker
experiments.comparison: Acts only after the MLP chooses to build a settlement
experiments.finding: Teacher-node match rose from 26.2% to 39.7%, but Value Base stayed 3/52 and the model still made weak build-timing decisions.
experiments.decision: Keep as a narrow component, not a whole-policy fix.

experiments.title: Longer settlement-head training
experiments.comparison: Two fresh matched mixed-bot screens
experiments.finding: Lower training loss and stronger label fit did not turn into more game wins; the longest run did slightly worse.
experiments.decision: Stop using extra epochs as the default remedy.

experiments.title: Dice-pip and development triggers
experiments.comparison: Same calibrated MLP and settlement head
experiments.finding: Choosing settlement nodes only by adjacent pips hurt. Buying a development card before End Turn with eight cards gained only two games.
experiments.decision: Neither rule cleared a convincing promotion bar.

experiments.title: Public-history action residual
experiments.comparison: Sixteen public events; fresh mixed-bot screen
experiments.finding: Teacher action agreement improved, yet the residual displaced winning choices. A state-only residual scored 20/64.
experiments.decision: Do not deploy this teacher-trained residual.

experiments.title: Bounded same-turn win scan
experiments.comparison: Fresh matched mixed-bot games, four screens
experiments.finding: Searching deterministic trade and build sequences to an immediate win flipped seven results toward the agent and none the other way in these screens.
experiments.decision: Promising low-cost tactical component; gain is small.

experiments.title: Backward loss counterfactuals
experiments.comparison: Six losses, 13 earlier decision states
experiments.finding: Two promising alternatives were End Turn versus maritime trade. Copied games contained true hidden cards, so these oracle values are not fair live-policy labels.
experiments.decision: Use only as diagnosis until belief-state sampling is implemented.

experiments.title: Trade-to-build invest/convert planner
experiments.comparison: Fresh web-bot confirmation; OneVOne scored 93/128
experiments.finding: Explicit legal trade→build search repaired resource conversion. The changing investment horizon lost three games to fixed horizon.
experiments.decision: Planning helps the MLP, but neither planner replaces OneVOne.

experiments.title: Planner inside OneVOne's main turn
experiments.comparison: Second fresh paired web-bot confirmation
experiments.finding: The planner rescued some OneVOne losses but reversed more of its wins during post-roll play.
experiments.decision: Leave OneVOne's main-turn decisions intact.

experiments.title: Tiny Transformer cloning OneVOne
experiments.comparison: Fresh web-bot games after teacher-action training
experiments.finding: Four prior observations raised held-out move agreement only 53.17%→53.41%. Cloning discarded the teacher's tactical calculation.
experiments.decision: Retain the heuristic as scaffold instead of replacing it with imitation.

experiments.title: Outcome Transformer beside OneVOne
experiments.comparison: 822 training games, 206 sealed boards × both seats
experiments.finding: The model changed 745 same-type moves. It gained 76 paired wins and lost 75; +1 overall is inconclusive despite held-out position AUC 0.8895.
experiments.decision: Keep plain OneVOne as incumbent.

experiments.title: Benjamin architecture on CPU
experiments.comparison: Native 15-VP R1 rules versus its fixed heuristic
experiments.finding: The CPU pipeline runs end to end, but this 256-teacher-game, 12,288-transition pilot did not improve wins.
experiments.decision: Treat as an architecture and throughput test, not a full-strength reproduction.

experiments.title: Benjamin CPU checkpoints on Catanatron
experiments.comparison: Pinned web bot; OneVOne scored 27/40 on same boards
experiments.finding: All actions were legal and games completed. The small checkpoint crossed a 15-VP-to-10-VP engine boundary with approximate opponent-hand features.
experiments.decision: Do not generalize this result to a fully trained native Benjamin agent.

experiments.title: Benjamin CPU pilot versus OneVOne
experiments.comparison: 25 random board seeds, both seats, zero errors or caps
experiments.finding: Benjamin averaged 3.16 VP and never built beyond its two setup settlements or a city. OneVOne averaged 10.20 VP.
experiments.decision: The transferred short-trained checkpoint is not competitive with OneVOne.

experiments.title: HexMachina published player and mechanism port
experiments.comparison: Small paired-seat compatibility probes
experiments.finding: The published player's direct field lookups did not fully match the local engine; its phase and resource heuristic were inactive after placement in this run. The mechanism port is an approximation.
experiments.decision: Use as comparison evidence, not proof of relative global strength.

experiments.title: FairValue policy
experiments.metric: 32 / 96 vs three Value bots; Value control 24 / 96
experiments.comparison: Four seats on 24 boards; AlphaBeta1 28/96 vs 27/96
experiments.finding: Connected sites, hand synergy, army and late development value helped against Value. The AlphaBeta1 difference was uncertain.
experiments.decision: Useful four-player heuristic base; separate from 1v1 results.

experiments.title: Initial standalone Transformer
experiments.comparison: Small four-player local pilot
experiments.finding: The learned policy alone did not convert enough resources or expand reliably.
experiments.decision: Use stronger policy structure and real games as the test.

experiments.title: Fair-policy guided search
experiments.comparison: Strong mixed table: 36/96 search vs 38/96 control
experiments.finding: Search beat the control consistently on the uniform AlphaBeta1 tier, but did not win more on the stronger mixed table.
experiments.decision: Keep as an opponent-specific candidate, not universal incumbent.

experiments.title: Transformer prior for guided search
experiments.comparison: Same 24-board search screen
experiments.finding: Differences were uncertain and inference cost rose; the learned root prior had no demonstrated strength benefit.
experiments.decision: Retain only as an ablation.

experiments.title: Tactical two-action VP scan
experiments.comparison: Five fresh confirmation tables; all 4,000 candidate/control games complete
experiments.finding: A deterministic visible trade/build scan delivered a board-clustered gain and survived direct comparison with its prior control.
experiments.decision: Promoted for the local four-player arena.

experiments.title: Last-seat opening pair
experiments.comparison: 16 boards, all seats, both opponent mixes
experiments.finding: The candidate changed legal fourth-seat openings but its paired interval crossed zero and its effect was limited to one seat.
experiments.decision: No promotion.

experiments.title: Road Building continuation
experiments.comparison: 24 fresh boards, all seats
experiments.finding: The action continuation worked and remained legal, but finished-game wins did not move in the strong table.
experiments.decision: No promotion.

experiments.title: Highest-VP robber victim
experiments.comparison: 24 fresh boards, all seats, paired controls
experiments.finding: Targeting the public VP leader gained in one mix and lost in the other; both intervals included zero.
experiments.decision: No promotion.

experiments.title: Heuristic rescue of model openings
experiments.comparison: FairValue control won 12/32; eight-board diverse mix
experiments.finding: Opening overrides improved VP but did not close the full model gap. Robber and trade/end overrides did not consistently improve wins.
experiments.decision: Focus diagnosis on later main-turn and discard choices.

experiments.title: External PPO policy on Catanatron
experiments.comparison: Same 16-board, four-seat schedule
experiments.finding: The transferred network ran legally and fast, but its policy alone was weaker after engine and observation translation.
experiments.decision: Do not infer the upstream full-agent strength from a policy-only port.

open_questions: What are the released competition rules, observation contract, runtime cap and opponent set?
Which action class causes the largest paired win loss: opening, road access, trade conversion, robber, development purchase or defense?
Can a win-trained state/action value model improve OneVOne without disturbing its tactical choices?
Can search sample hidden states from public evidence and beat the incumbent on fresh boards?
